title: Lattice and Text to Lattice documentation register

authority.claimBoundary: This register describes the Lattice method at an architectural level and the bounded Text to Lattice implementation evidenced in this repository. It does not redistribute the exclusive register profile, certify universal conformance, or convert source tests into deployed proof.
authority.changePolicy: Stable identifiers persist. A claim changes here with cited evidence; a rendered filter, expansion, or downloaded view never changes authoritative state.
authority.marginalValuePolicy: Treat consequence multiplied by plausibility multiplied by lifecycle value as the decision boundary. Unusual findings remain eligible; low-consequence, implausible, lifecycle-poor work does not become release-blocking by novelty alone.
authority.exportPolicy: Markdown and HTML are deterministic projections of this register. Filtered browser exports are nonauthoritative reading views.

conceptMap.description: A typed map of the upstream Lattice engine: who supplies authority, how meaning becomes a bounded output plan, how candidates clear protected gates, and where hosts and ecosystem applications remain responsible.

groups.label: Authority
groups.description: The caller and domain sources that establish meaning before expression.

groups.label: Semantic contract
groups.description: Typed atoms and relations that make preservation testable.

groups.label: Context and plan
groups.description: Explicit context, content layers, representations, priorities, and requested outputs.

groups.label: Realization
groups.description: Mapped proposals and the controlled literal baseline.

groups.label: Evaluation
groups.description: Engine gates, profile decisions, and deterministic selection.

groups.label: Output and evidence
groups.description: Plain-text results, receipts, and structural verification.

groups.label: Host boundary
groups.description: Presentation, source quality, privacy, and human review that stay outside the engine.

groups.label: Ecosystem
groups.description: Products that apply or interpret Lattice under their own contracts.

nodes.label: Lattice engine
nodes.caption: Meaning contract ≠ register ≠ realization ≠ presentation
nodes.definition: A local-first deterministic TypeScript engine that realizes and validates context-sensitive plain text from typed meaning, explicit context, declarative profiles, and traceable candidates.

nodes.label: Caller and domain authority
nodes.caption: Truth enters before expression
nodes.definition: The caller supplies structured claims, terminology, context, candidate provenance, and domain attestations. Lattice does not infer source truth, authority, or missing high-priority context.

nodes.label: Meaning contract
nodes.caption: Semantic authority in typed form
nodes.definition: A bounded contract gives each semantic obligation a stable identity, frame, criticality, delivery policy, protected fields, permitted evidence, and prohibited dependencies.

nodes.label: Semantic atoms
nodes.caption: Independently addressable obligations
nodes.definition: Actions, states, timings, conditions, consequences, prohibitions, uncertainties, recovery steps, and relations carry structured subjects, predicates, objects, polarity, modality, value, unit, and condition references.

nodes.label: Typed relations
nodes.caption: Before · after · requires · causes · contradicts
nodes.definition: Relations connect existing atoms and make protected order, dependency, causality, and contradiction explicit; unresolved references, invalid self-links, and incoherent cycles fail closed.

nodes.label: Register context
nodes.caption: Explicit, never ambient
nodes.definition: Domain, surface, mode, stakes, safety class, locale, audience, focalizer, channel capabilities, and execution limits arrive as validated input rather than time, locale, identity, network, or prior-run inference.

nodes.label: Content layer
nodes.caption: Operative · experiential · interpretive
nodes.definition: A requested layer determines which atoms must be explicit or may be inferable, while experiential and interpretive emphasis cannot contradict or conceal operative meaning.

nodes.label: Representation
nodes.caption: Standard · accessibility-equivalent
nodes.definition: Accessibility is another realization of the same relevant atoms, not a fourth narrative layer. Essential meaning cannot depend on unavailable imagery, color, sound, spatial inference, timing perception, or implication.

nodes.label: Protected priority
nodes.caption: Safety before ornament
nodes.definition: Safety, semantic fidelity, accessibility equivalence, required operative clarity, and authoritative domain correctness are hard gates that profile style and ranking cannot outweigh.

nodes.label: Profile and RSR boundary
nodes.caption: Declarative policy · protected license
nodes.definition: Profiles declare bounded predicates, validators, dependencies, conflicts, and lower-priority policy without executable transforms. The bundled Relational Systems Register remains separately licensed and is not reproduced here.

nodes.label: Output plan
nodes.caption: Requested layer × representation
nodes.definition: Normalized outputs are unique, ordered layer-and-representation pairs; accessibility equivalents pull in their standard pair, and safety-critical contexts require both operative representations.

nodes.label: Mapped candidate
nodes.caption: Untrusted proposal with atom evidence
nodes.definition: A host may propose bounded plain text, atom identifiers, and validation metadata. Candidate order and source do not authorize selection; unknown mappings and invented claims remain rejectable.

nodes.label: Literal baseline
nodes.caption: Controlled fallback, labeled literal
nodes.definition: When no mapped candidate targets an output, the engine constructs a deterministic realization from controlled literal forms or structured frames and never labels it full conformance.

nodes.label: Hard gates
nodes.caption: Failure cannot be averaged away
nodes.definition: Engine-owned checks reject uncovered atoms, protected drift, changed polarity or modality, quantity or unit change, unsafe dependencies, layer contradiction, accessibility gaps, and other registered structural failures.

nodes.label: Profile evaluation
nodes.caption: Applicability ≠ result
nodes.definition: Each rule records applied, suppressed, or inapplicable separately from pass, warn, fail, unknown, or not-applicable, so nonexecution cannot masquerade as satisfaction.

nodes.label: Lexicographic selection
nodes.caption: Priority tuple, then stable digest
nodes.definition: Admissible candidates are ranked lexicographically by protected priority, conformance, registered findings, and stable tie-break evidence; a stylistic gain cannot compensate for a hard failure.

nodes.label: Layered plain-text output
nodes.caption: Selected realization with bounded conformance
nodes.definition: Each output exposes its layer, representation, text, atom mapping, candidate source, conformance, coverage, findings, and rule decisions; the host still owns presentation.

nodes.label: Derivation receipt
nodes.caption: Reproducibility, not authenticity
nodes.definition: A canonical receipt binds input, engine and profile versions, outputs, candidates, decisions, assurance scope, and derivation digest without claiming that facts or history are authentic.

nodes.label: Structural verification
nodes.caption: Self-consistent, unauthenticated
nodes.definition: Receipt and result verification reject unsupported schemas, broken references, altered aggregates, and digest tampering while reporting that integrity is self-consistent and not externally authenticated.

nodes.label: Host application
nodes.caption: Candidate, UI, privacy, and persistence owner
nodes.definition: The host owns domain-source quality, mapped candidate production, sanitization, rendering, storage consent, privacy, interface accessibility, and any claims beyond the engine's declared trust scope.

nodes.label: Human and assistive-technology review
nodes.caption: Empirical judgment remains necessary
nodes.definition: Disabled users, assistive technologies, domain reviewers, and editors test accessibility, comprehension, truth, moral adequacy, and literary quality that deterministic structure cannot prove.

nodes.label: Text to Lattice
nodes.caption: Probabilistic wrapper, distinct authority model
nodes.definition: The hah.dev demonstrator infers a bounded contract from prose with local models and independent checks. It does not inherit the upstream engine's typed caller-authority guarantee and must state its weaker semantic boundary separately.

nodes.label: FOG OF SEA
nodes.caption: Naval learning and operational uncertainty
nodes.definition: A host context that applies Lattice to naval learning, operational uncertainty, and accessible tactical interaction under its own domain and evidence responsibilities.

nodes.label: CHORUS
nodes.caption: Social and epistemic systems
nodes.definition: A host context that applies Lattice to social and epistemic systems while retaining its own simulation, claim, accessibility, and evidence boundaries.

nodes.label: Evenward
nodes.caption: Selected embodied guidance and care
nodes.definition: A host context that selectively applies Lattice to embodied guidance and care while remaining responsible for safety, privacy, presentation, and human validation.

skillMap.methodNote: This map adapts NN/g's competency-mapping form to an evidence inventory for the upstream Lattice engine at revision d6cc85b. It never rates a person, team member, or human proficiency. A score records the strongest evidence class for a system capability, not importance or artistic quality.

scale.label: Not claimed
scale.definition: The capability is outside the authorized product boundary or lacks a supported claim.

scale.label: Defined
scale.definition: A bounded requirement and intended evidence path exist.

scale.label: Implemented
scale.definition: Repository implementation exists; verification or lifecycle evidence remains incomplete.

scale.label: Internally verified
scale.definition: Maintainer-authored repository tests verify ordinary and boundary behavior.

scale.label: Adversarially verified
scale.definition: Self-authored adversarial repository evidence challenges realistic failure and tampering modes.

scale.label: Externally validated
scale.definition: Independent, production, longitudinal, or representative user evidence supports the claim across contexts.

capabilities.label: Semantic and relational modeling
capabilities.definition: Models independently identified atoms, protected frame fields, delivery obligations, terminology, prohibited claims, and before, after, requires, causes, and contradicts relations.
capabilities.evidence: The semantic core rejects unresolved conditions, invalid relation targets, contradictions, ordering cycles, and weakened protected meaning; adversarial fixtures challenge polarity, modality, quantity, units, uncertainty, order, and recovery.
capabilities.openBoundary: Typed contracts make declared meaning testable but do not prove source facts or interpret arbitrary prose.

capabilities.label: Context and audience modeling
capabilities.definition: Requires explicit domain, surface, mode, stakes, safety class, locale, audience, focalizer, channel, scene, and bounded execution context.
capabilities.evidence: Context validation rejects missing or unsupported high-priority values, bounds tags and limits, and never consults ambient identity, time, locale, network, or previous runs.
capabilities.openBoundary: Correctness still depends on the caller supplying adequate and truthful context; English-oriented resources limit locale scope.

capabilities.label: Layered content architecture
capabilities.definition: Keeps operative, experiential, and interpretive content obligations separate while allowing multiple representations of the same atoms.
capabilities.evidence: Output normalization, required-atom planning, cross-output checks, and adversarial layer-contradiction cases enforce the distinction.
capabilities.openBoundary: The engine evaluates supplied structured candidates; it does not generate novel literary prose or infer a layer from free-form text.

capabilities.label: Register and constraint architecture
capabilities.definition: Compiles versioned declarative profiles with bounded predicates, known validators, dependencies, conflicts, priorities, enforcement, and protected engine namespaces.
capabilities.evidence: Compilation rejects unknown fields, executable or unknown validators, cycles, undeclared conflicts, same-tier hard conflicts, protected priorities, and unresolved dependencies.
capabilities.openBoundary: A structurally valid profile is not proof of artistic quality; the bundled RSR remains separately licensed and is not inventoried here.

capabilities.label: Deterministic and bounded engineering
capabilities.definition: Normalizes bounded plain data, freezes compiled structures, ranks lexicographically, and excludes time, filesystem order, platform locale, network state, and ambient randomness from realization.
capabilities.evidence: Canonical digests, stable ordering, explicit execution limits, candidate-order invariance, and repeated adversarial requests demonstrate byte-identical derivation within the reviewed revision.
capabilities.openBoundary: Determinism holds for canonical requests and pinned engine/profile versions; hosts and external candidate producers need their own controls.

capabilities.label: Core security and trust boundary
capabilities.definition: Accepts bounded nonexecutable data, prevents profiles from rewriting semantic slots or running arbitrary code, rejects prohibited structures, and performs no runtime network, telemetry, or hidden persistence.
capabilities.evidence: Plain-data validation, restricted predicate syntax, known validator registration, protected priorities, fail-closed errors, and adversarial malformed-input cases exercise the core boundary.
capabilities.openBoundary: Hosts still own parsing duplicate-key rejection, output escaping, candidate trust, storage permission, network behavior, and UI security.

capabilities.label: Accessibility equivalence
capabilities.definition: Models accessibility-equivalent output as a representation of the same relevant atoms and suppresses imagery, color, sound, spatial, timing-perception, or implication dependencies where unavailable.
capabilities.evidence: Context protection, output normalization, atom delivery, hard gates, and cross-output parity are implemented and covered by maintainer-authored tests.
capabilities.openBoundary: Structural channel independence does not replace testing with disabled users, assistive technologies, or the host interface.

capabilities.label: Evidence and provenance
capabilities.definition: Records canonical inputs, versioned dependencies, candidate decisions, atom coverage, rule dispositions, findings, output digests, trust scope, and a reproducible derivation digest.
capabilities.evidence: Receipt and result verifiers enforce exact schemas, referential consistency, aggregate conformance, output binding, and tamper detection in adversarial fixtures.
capabilities.openBoundary: The receipt is self-consistent and unauthenticated; hashes do not establish truth, authorship, or historical authenticity.

capabilities.label: Adversarial verification
capabilities.definition: Challenges realistic contract, profile, candidate, ordering, accessibility, tampering, execution-bound, locale, and trust-scope failures rather than counting happy paths alone.
capabilities.evidence: The reviewed adversarial suite exercises candidate exhaustion, protected meaning, conflicts, malformed records, candidate-order independence, receipt tampering, and bounded failure behavior.
capabilities.openBoundary: The suite is self-authored repository evidence, not independent security review, formal proof, or production observation.

capabilities.label: Lifecycle and host integration
capabilities.definition: Uses stable versions, schemas, identifiers, profile digests, typed failures, verification functions, CLI boundaries, and explicit host duties to make integration and supersession inspectable.
capabilities.evidence: Architecture and requirements define extension, failure, verification, and host contracts; the reviewed engine exposes structured results and verification rather than presentation-side assertions.
capabilities.openBoundary: No score five is assigned: independent integration, production, longitudinal maintenance, and representative user evidence remain external.

serviceBlueprint.scenario: A visitor converts authorized prose into one bounded Lattice outcome in the résumé demonstrator.
serviceBlueprint.actor: A visitor using a secure, JavaScript-capable browser with Unicode segmentation, WebGPU, and sufficient local storage.
serviceBlueprint.goal: Receive a materially revised, locally checked result; an unchanged context-bounded clearance; a review-marked draft; one precise clarification; or an honest refusal without transmitting prose to the lease service.
serviceBlueprint.methodNote: The blueprint follows NN/g's service-blueprint separation of user action, visible service, backstage process, and support process, then adds evidence and data-boundary rows because trust and recovery are part of this service.

lines.label: Line of interaction
lines.meaning: What the visitor directly acts upon and what the interface returns.

lines.label: Line of visibility
lines.meaning: What is disclosed as status or outcome versus what remains internal pipeline work.

lines.label: Line of trust and network
lines.meaning: The only crossings are bounded attestation, lease metadata, and revision-pinned model assets; prose stays local.

lines.label: Line of accountability
lines.meaning: Source and tests support repository claims; deployment, provider measurement, and manual exercises require separate evidence.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Govern the method, licensed profile boundary, version, and authorized conformance claims.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: A cited upstream revision, applicable license terms, and an explicit public claim boundary.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep input, interaction, local pipeline, accessibility, privacy, teardown, and public outcome behavior aligned with the requirements.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Exact source revision, automated contracts, manual interaction matrix, and built static artifact inspection.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Approve exact model, tokenizer, runtime, and WASM revisions plus their integrity, provenance, and license boundary.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Pinned URLs and versions, tokenizer hashes, fetched artifact record, licenses, and a recorded disposition for the WASM provenance gap.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Operate request safety, secrets, signed credentials, exact admission, lifecycle accounting, alarms, retention, and fail-closed capacity policy.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Reviewed Worker revision, binding and secret-name inventory, deployed route evidence, provider metrics, and bounded load results.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep the dedicated static frame, origin policy, message protocol, CSP, provider action, and teardown boundary exact.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Deployed header capture, route and origin inspection, protocol tests, provider hostname/action evidence, and accessibility exercise.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Publish complete no-JavaScript semantics, deterministic projections, working links, escaped register content, and matching integrity metadata.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Documentation drift check, SHA-256 manifest, generated-page inspection, and static-route test results.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Accept or reject residuals and approve only the exact source, configuration, artifacts, provider controls, and evidence that were reviewed.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Dated gate record naming the revision and artifact digests, with every open exception assigned or explicitly deferred.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Use text they are authorized to process, choose whether to download large local models, and decide whether the published device and provider residuals are acceptable.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Visible purpose, size, privacy, capability, provider, outcome, and residual disclosures before consequential action.

stages.visitorAction: Opens Text to Lattice and reads the purpose, limits, privacy caution, and capability requirements.
stages.frontstage: The dialog names a local, bounded demonstration and keeps the canonical documentation path available.
stages.backstage: The interface probes secure context, Unicode segmentation, WebGPU, storage estimate, and cached-model state.
stages.supportNetwork: No service call and no model download occurs during source preflight or capability explanation.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Unsupported capability yields a precise unavailable state and preserves access to the semantic documentation page.
stages.dataCrossing: Capability metadata remains in the browser; no prose exists yet.
stages.failure: A browser cannot support the runtime or cannot establish a secure context.
stages.recovery: Read the method and limitation record; use a compatible browser or device without losing entered work.

stages.visitorAction: Enters one to 700 Unicode-aware words and chooses Convert.
stages.frontstage: The shared counter, inline validation, and concise status expose only actionable limits.
stages.backstage: The host validates control characters, Unicode structure, 12,000 code units, passage count, initial work groups, clarification limits, and completion ceilings before requesting capacity.
stages.supportNetwork: None; admission and model systems remain untouched until complete preflight succeeds.
stages.evidenceRecovery: The source stays editable. Rejection is local, bounded, and does not truncate or relabel text.
stages.dataCrossing: Source and structural findings stay in the browser document.
stages.failure: Input exceeds a published boundary or contains unsafe structure.
stages.recovery: Revise the source locally; no quota was consumed.

stages.visitorAction: Continues through human verification when the service requires it.
stages.frontstage: A dedicated verification surface reports pending, interactive, completed, limited, or unavailable state.
stages.backstage: The parent creates a fresh correlation identifier, accepts only the exact frame origin and Window, then requests a lease with no request body.
stages.supportNetwork: The verify.hah.dev frame obtains one Turnstile token; the lease Worker validates request safety, secrets, challenge, exact global admission, visitor eligibility, and lease state.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Bounded Retry-After values become a local retry ETA; every terminal path removes the frame and stale listeners.
stages.dataCrossing: Only closed attestation messages, a token, request metadata, an opaque signed cookie, and lease credentials cross. Source, clarification, candidate, and output do not.
stages.failure: Verification rejects, the global or visitor budget is ineligible, or the support service is unavailable.
stages.recovery: Fail closed, show a bounded reason or ETA, and leave canonical documentation public.

stages.visitorAction: Waits while actual preparation progress is announced and may cancel.
stages.frontstage: The interface reports real generator or verifier loading progress without simulated delay.
stages.backstage: A dedicated worker installs its network boundary before importing model libraries, validates closed RPC, loads one role at a time, and disables WebLLM's IndexedDB cache path. Public model cache may remain and contains no prose.
stages.supportNetwork: Only manifest-enumerated, revision-pinned HTTPS model shards, tokenizers, and WASM assets may be requested with credentials omitted and no referrer.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Cancel interrupts generation, terminates the worker when necessary, and releases the lease through bounded idempotent handling.
stages.dataCrossing: Pinned asset requests reveal ordinary network metadata and selected public model revisions; prose is not part of any URL, header, or asset body.
stages.failure: Storage, WebGPU, CORS, pinned assets, upstream availability, or runtime preparation fails.
stages.recovery: Unload local runtime, release capacity, and return unavailable without candidate text.

stages.visitorAction: Reads bounded progress; no additional action is required unless ambiguity is material.
stages.frontstage: Status names analysis rather than claiming completion.
stages.backstage: Lossless passages are serialized as inert JSON, analyzed without clarification history, schema-checked, host-normalized, and checked against evidence spans and context budgets.
stages.supportNetwork: No support service receives model prompts or prose; inference runs inside the browser worker.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Malformed, oversized, mismatched, or under-evidenced analysis is rejected before it can authorize drafting.
stages.dataCrossing: Source crosses the document-to-worker boundary through closed RPC; it does not cross the browser network boundary.
stages.failure: The model cannot return a complete, closed, evidence-linked analysis within fixed budgets.
stages.recovery: Return unable-to-attempt, or ask one provenance-bound clarification when the analyzer identifies a resolvable ambiguity.

stages.visitorAction: Answers one short, enumerated clarification when asked, or continues waiting for a draft.
stages.frontstage: The interface exposes only a precise host-normalized question and bounded answer controls; candidate text remains hidden.
stages.backstage: One exact matching answer authorizes one analyzer recheck. The generator drafts a material candidate subject to protected spans, semantic obligations, word materiality, and fixed completion budgets.
stages.supportNetwork: Lease renewal may extend bounded capacity; its request carries the credential but no prose.
stages.evidenceRecovery: A repeated question cannot become acceptance. A draft that merely changes punctuation, casing, or spacing is not material.
stages.dataCrossing: Clarification and draft remain inside the browser and local worker; renewal metadata alone crosses the network.
stages.failure: Ambiguity remains, provenance mismatches, or no material candidate can be produced safely.
stages.recovery: Return needs-clarification or unable-to-attempt without exposing a candidate-dependent trace.

stages.visitorAction: Waits through explicit verification and bounded repair states.
stages.frontstage: The interface reports checking, repair, or certification without presenting rejected work as a result.
stages.backstage: A distinct verifier model, deterministic validators, post-candidate re-atomization, bounded repair, and whole-document certification test fidelity, coverage, domain correctness, accessibility, clarity, register fit, and materiality.
stages.supportNetwork: No verifier finding, atom identifier, candidate, or certification record leaves the browser.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Rejected candidates are withheld. The public projection removes candidate-dependent identifiers, counts, layers, and issue categories.
stages.dataCrossing: Candidate data crosses only the closed document-to-worker boundary; support services receive no semantic content.
stages.failure: A release gate fails, budgets exhaust, or a lower-priority issue remains.
stages.recovery: Repair within fixed ceilings; otherwise return review-required when semantically releasable or unable-to-attempt with one host-authored record.

stages.visitorAction: Reads the outcome, copies nothing through routine controls, then dismisses or starts over.
stages.frontstage: The interface presents exactly one outcome state, explicit limitation, and protected result region; it never calls review-required complete clearance.
stages.backstage: The host keeps output transient, conceals it on blur, page invisibility, print, and detectable Print Screen events, and tears down model and modal state on exit.
stages.supportNetwork: The browser releases the opaque lease with bounded idempotent retries; the global authority updates lifecycle state and expiry alarms.
stages.evidenceRecovery: A release failure remains bounded and retryable. Static HTML, Markdown, JSON, JSON-LD, sitemap, and llms surfaces remain available when the service fails closed.
stages.dataCrossing: Release credentials and operation identifiers may cross; result text stays transient in browser memory and is never sent to the lease service or static evidence surfaces.
stages.failure: Output capture cannot be fully prevented, release can race unload, or the remote authority can be unavailable.
stages.recovery: State is torn down locally; lease expiry is the final backstop. Documentation states that browser, operating-system, camera, and assistive-technology capture cannot be guaranteed away.

securityModel.scope: The browser wrapper, isolated model worker, dedicated verification frame, public lease endpoint, global usage authority, pinned model-asset origins, and generated documentation surfaces.
securityModel.method: Threats are release-relevant when consequence, plausibility, and lifecycle value together justify action. Each entry separates as-built controls from pre-publication evidence and from the residual boundary that the browser or provider cannot erase.

assets.label: Source, clarification, candidate, and result text
Model, tokenizer, WASM, and runtime integrity
Accessible public evidence and honest limitations

trustBoundaries.label: Visitor ↔ résumé interface
trustBoundaries.crossing: Untrusted prose and interaction events enter a semantic React surface.

trustBoundaries.label: Document ↔ isolated model worker
trustBoundaries.crossing: Closed RPC carries bounded inert model data and validated responses.

trustBoundaries.label: Model worker ↔ pinned asset origins
trustBoundaries.crossing: Only enumerated HTTPS model, tokenizer, and WASM assets may cross.

trustBoundaries.label: Résumé origin ↔ verify.hah.dev frame
trustBoundaries.crossing: Closed postMessage schemas carry correlation state and an attestation token, never prose.

trustBoundaries.label: Browser ↔ lease Worker and global authority
trustBoundaries.crossing: No-body acquisition plus authenticated lifecycle calls govern capacity without semantic content.

trustBoundaries.label: Source register ↔ generated public documentation
trustBoundaries.crossing: Escaped deterministic projections expose claims and citations but no private profile inventory or visitor content.

threats.title: Prose crosses a network boundary
threats.vector: A URL, header, request body, telemetry hook, attestation message, or error report incorporates source, clarification, candidate, or result text.
threats.consequence: Private or sensitive prose leaves the visitor's browser and contradicts the core privacy claim.
threats.plausibility: Realistic whenever a model runtime, verification provider, or usage service performs network work.
threats.lifecycleValue: A single enforced data-flow boundary is reusable across every pipeline stage and dependency revision.
threats.classificationRationale: High consequence, ordinary integration plausibility, and architectural reuse make this release-blocking.
asBuilt: The official lease acquisition has no request body and the published policy forbids source transmission.
Model asset URLs and headers are constant, enumerated, credentialless, and independent of user content.
The attestation protocol uses closed messages without source or output.
requiredBeforePublication: Exercise production network traces for acquisition, renewal, release, asset fetches, errors, and verification.
Confirm CSP and deployed telemetry configuration do not add unmodeled egress.
residualBoundary: IP address, user agent, timing, public model choice, and ordinary transport metadata remain visible to contacted providers.
The repository test suite is not a capture of deployed traffic.

threats.title: Hostile prose acquires authority or execution
threats.vector: Prompt injection, control characters, bidi abuse, HTML-like content, or model-authored issue text becomes an instruction, executable markup, or public authority.
threats.consequence: The pipeline can ignore its contract, misrepresent a finding, execute injected content, or expose unsafe markup.
threats.plausibility: Directly plausible because arbitrary prose is the intended input.
threats.lifecycleValue: Inert serialization and text-only rendering protect every future model and document revision.
threats.classificationRationale: The input channel is necessarily hostile, so containment is a primary release boundary.
asBuilt: Complete Unicode and structural preflight precedes lease acquisition and model load.
System instructions are separated from escaped JSON user data and constrained by closed schemas.
Public findings are host-authored and React renders visitor and model text as text nodes.
requiredBeforePublication: Re-run injection, Unicode, recursive noninterference, and generated-document escaping checks on the release artifact.
Review any new renderer or model transport for HTML interpretation or dynamic authority.
residualBoundary: A local model can still misunderstand inert data; later release gates, not prompt wording alone, contain that risk.

threats.title: Semantic drift is released as success
threats.vector: Generation drops, invents, negates, broadens, narrows, or reorders a material obligation and a correlated checker accepts the candidate.
threats.consequence: Safety instructions, conditions, quantities, uncertainty, causality, consequences, or recovery relationships can change while the interface claims successful transformation.
threats.plausibility: Probabilistic generation makes drift realistic even under structured output.
threats.lifecycleValue: Independent verification, deterministic sentinels, and honest withholding remain useful across model upgrades.
threats.classificationRationale: Meaning preservation is the product's central consequence; an incorrect success is worse than a refusal.
asBuilt: Protected spans and semantic sentinels preserve explicit high-consequence content.
A distinct verifier, deterministic validators, re-atomization, repair, and whole-document certification gate release.
Five outcome states prevent withheld or unresolved work from being relabeled as complete.
requiredBeforePublication: Run the full adversarial and semantic regression corpus against exact release revisions.
Record manual review across realistic genres without treating those samples as universal proof.
residualBoundary: No bounded corpus or model pair proves equivalence for all prose.
Review-required is semantically releasable but explicitly not complete bounded clearance.

threats.title: Input or inference exhausts browser resources
threats.vector: Pathological Unicode, dense passages, oversized tokens, retry subdivision, completion loops, worker queues, or memory pressure trigger unbounded local work.
threats.consequence: The page stalls, a device becomes unstable, accessibility degrades, or capacity remains occupied without useful work.
threats.plausibility: Realistic for arbitrary prose and multi-gigabyte browser models, especially on constrained devices.
threats.lifecycleValue: Central ceilings and early preflight bound new pipeline stages as the implementation evolves.
threats.classificationRationale: Common resource variability and meaningful reliability consequences justify fixing and testing the boundary now.
asBuilt: Word, code-unit, grapheme, token, control, passage, batch, executed-group, context, completion, queue, and response ceilings are explicit.
Preflight completes before lease or model load, and worker operations have timeouts and cancellation paths.
requiredBeforePublication: Measure representative supported devices for memory, storage, cancellation, thermal load, and worst-case completion time.
Verify deployed limits match the documented constants after bundling.
residualBoundary: WebGPU drivers and browser memory management remain outside application control.
A supported capability probe cannot guarantee stable inference on every device.

threats.title: Pinned supply-chain artifact is substituted or unusable
threats.vector: A model shard, tokenizer, WASM binary, runtime package, CDN response, or upstream license changes or is served contrary to the reviewed revision.
threats.consequence: Inference semantics, code execution, availability, or redistribution authority can diverge from the reviewed build.
threats.plausibility: Revision pinning lowers accidental drift but third-party hosting, binary provenance, and model-use terms remain realistic dependencies.
threats.lifecycleValue: One manifest and provenance gate scales across upgrades and incident response.
threats.classificationRationale: Executable third-party artifacts cross a privileged boundary; the WASM provenance gap and the public-prose model-use disposition remain open.
asBuilt: Models, runtime versions, tokenizer hashes, WASM commit, and exact asset paths are pinned in source.
The worker installs its request policy before loading model modules and rejects unexpected transports.
The model contract links the Llama 3.2 community license and acceptable-use policy without treating those links as approval.
requiredBeforePublication: Resolve or explicitly accept the pinned WASM binary license and provenance boundary before public enablement.
Record an owner-approved Llama 3.2 license and acceptable-use disposition for arbitrary public prose.
Fetch, hash, archive, and compare release artifacts through the authorized supply-chain process.
residualBoundary: The source currently records that standalone license metadata is absent from the pinned binary repository.
Source pins do not establish binary reproducibility or resolve the Llama acceptable-use and licensing decision.

threats.title: Cross-origin attestation is forged, replayed, or confused
threats.vector: A sibling frame, stale token, mismatched hostname/action, guessed correlation identifier, unexpected message shape, or replayed attestation reaches grant accounting.
threats.consequence: Automated or cross-site traffic can consume scarce capacity or bind verification to the wrong visitor flow.
threats.plausibility: Cross-origin messaging and bearer tokens create a routine web attack surface.
threats.lifecycleValue: A closed versioned protocol and server-side binding remain reusable if the provider or frame changes.
threats.classificationRationale: The boundary protects shared availability and credential authenticity with realistic web vectors.
asBuilt: The parent checks exact origin, exact Window source, protocol version, closed keys, and a fresh 144-bit correlation identifier.
The server validates hostname, action, freshness, and single use before grant accounting; every terminal path removes the frame.
requiredBeforePublication: Verify production frame headers, origin routing, site key, action, hostname, and replay storage with real provider responses.
Exercise keyboard and assistive-technology behavior for interactive challenges.
residualBoundary: Provider availability, accessibility, fraud scoring, and privacy practices remain external dependencies.

threats.title: Lease or accounting state is abused
threats.vector: Forged, expired, replayed, cross-method, cross-owner, or concurrently mutated credentials cause duplicate grants, stolen renewals, missed releases, or inconsistent counts.
threats.consequence: One visitor can monopolize capacity, legitimate work can be denied, or the global authority can drift from real lifecycle state.
threats.plausibility: Any public signed-credential lifecycle is exposed to replay and concurrency races.
threats.lifecycleValue: Exact state transitions and one global authority simplify every future quota policy.
threats.classificationRationale: Shared capacity depends on exact lifecycle integrity under ordinary concurrency and hostile replay.
asBuilt: Distinct HMAC secrets bind visitor cookies and lease credentials; canonical encoding, expiry, method, and actor checks precede state work.
One globally named SQLite-backed Durable Object serializes exact admissions, grants, renewals, releases, ownership, and expiry.
requiredBeforePublication: Deploy with independent encrypted secrets and exercise concurrent production transitions, alarm recovery, and secret rotation.
Confirm idempotent client release behavior against deployed Retry-After variants.
residualBoundary: Provider point-in-time recovery may retain pseudonymous state for the published recovery window.
Network loss can leave a lease until bounded expiry even when local teardown succeeds.

threats.title: Distributed traffic exhausts the free-tier budget
threats.vector: Requests distributed across IPs or Cloudflare locations invoke the public Worker before in-Worker shaping and exceed the accounting assumptions.
threats.consequence: The demonstrator fails closed for legitimate visitors or consumes shared account capacity; other static evidence must remain available.
threats.plausibility: Plausible for any public endpoint; location-local permissive counters cannot guarantee an aggregate Worker-invocation ceiling.
threats.lifecycleValue: Separating exact downstream accounting from best-effort edge shedding prevents false capacity claims in later deployments.
threats.classificationRationale: The free-tier boundary is consequential and the provider architecture leaves a known distributed-traffic gap.
asBuilt: Exact global minute and UTC-day admission precedes Siteverify and lifecycle work; visitor, grant, and active-lease caps protect downstream resources.
Ingress, method, path, and credential shapers shed local load, while policy states they do not guarantee billed invocation limits.
Quota exhaustion fails closed and static semantic pages remain unrestricted.
requiredBeforePublication: Install and verify the required path-scoped edge rule before public enablement.
Measure Worker, Durable Object, row, alarm, CPU, storage, and cross-location traffic in the provider dashboard; recalculate carryover from observed latency.
residualBoundary: The Cloudflare Free plan does not provide an exact in-application bound on all hostile Worker invocations.
Distributed adversarial traffic remains outside the published deterministic budget proof.

threats.title: Generated output is captured despite interface friction
threats.vector: Selection APIs, clipboard events, printing, page capture, browser extensions, developer tools, accessibility APIs, operating-system screenshots, cameras, or memory inspection obtain result text.
threats.consequence: A visitor or third party retains output despite the interface's deterrent treatment, and an overstated claim would mislead users about control.
threats.plausibility: Browser event controls can block routine paths, but privileged and out-of-band capture is always plausible.
threats.lifecycleValue: An honest limitation prevents future styling or browser changes from becoming a false security promise.
threats.classificationRationale: The privacy consequence is meaningful, but bespoke escalation cannot close the browser and operating-system boundary; the bounded fix is deterrence plus precise disclosure.
asBuilt: Routine selection, copy, cut, drag, context menu, touch callout, and print paths are disabled for generated output.
Visibility, blur, print, and detectable Print Screen events conceal output behind a reduced-motion-compatible veil.
Semantic access is preserved and the canonical limitation rejects guarantees of capture prevention or AI unreadability.
requiredBeforePublication: Manually exercise keyboard, touch, print, visibility, blur, reduced-motion, forced-colors, and assistive-technology paths.
Review copy after each control change so deterrence is never described as prevention.
residualBoundary: Browser, extension, operating-system, accessibility, camera, and physical observation remain outside application control.
Additional anti-capture complexity can reduce accessibility while failing to remove the residual risk.

threats.title: Release or configuration drift invalidates the documented model
threats.vector: Bundled constants, Worker secrets, routes, CSP, edge rules, model revisions, provider bindings, generated documents, or deployed artifacts diverge from the reviewed register.
threats.consequence: Controls exist in source but not in production, public evidence becomes stale, or a release claim silently exceeds its proof.
threats.plausibility: Configuration drift is routine across independent origins, Workers, static export, and third-party artifacts.
threats.lifecycleValue: Deterministic generation, drift checks, explicit gates, and traceable identifiers reduce every later release review.
threats.classificationRationale: The architecture spans several independent release surfaces, making drift both plausible and consequential.
asBuilt: Requirements use stable identifiers and this documentation is deterministically generated with SHA-256 manifests.
Model, protocol, endpoint, and policy constants are centralized and source-tested.
requiredBeforePublication: Run build, lint, type, full test, documentation drift, static-artifact inspection, and secret-name checks from the exact release tree.
Verify both origins, Worker routes, CSP, bindings, edge rules, provider limits, and public links after deployment.
residualBoundary: A repository manifest proves bytes in one tree, not remote deployment identity or provider configuration.
Manual and operational evidence must be dated and renewed after consequential change.

prePublicationGates.label: Exact release artifact
prePublicationGates.requirement: Build, lint, type-check, full tests, documentation drift, static route, and generated-worker inspections pass from the exact release tree.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Dated command transcript and artifact digests.

prePublicationGates.label: Production origin and secret boundary
prePublicationGates.requirement: hah.dev, verify.hah.dev, Worker routes, CSP, bindings, and distinct encrypted secrets match the documented protocol.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Deployed configuration inspection without secret disclosure.

prePublicationGates.label: Edge and provider capacity controls
prePublicationGates.requirement: The required path-scoped edge rule is active and provider-side CPU, storage, request, row, alarm, latency, and distributed-traffic measurements support the budget.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Provider configuration record and bounded load evidence.

prePublicationGates.label: Supply-chain provenance and model-use approval
prePublicationGates.requirement: Pinned model, tokenizer, runtime, and WASM bytes are verified; the standalone WASM license and provenance boundary is resolved or explicitly accepted; and the Llama 3.2 license and acceptable-use disposition for arbitrary public prose is recorded.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Hashes, source or archive record, licenses, acceptable-use review, and owner decisions.

prePublicationGates.label: Manual interaction and accessibility
prePublicationGates.requirement: Keyboard, screen reader, touch, 400 percent zoom, reduced motion, forced colors, print, cancellation, blur, and a second browser engine complete the critical paths.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Dated manual matrix with failures and dispositions.

prePublicationGates.label: Production privacy trace
prePublicationGates.requirement: Network traces show no source, clarification, candidate, verifier finding, or output in lease, attestation, model-asset, error, or telemetry traffic.
prePublicationGates.evidenceNeeded: Sanitized trace inventory from both origins and supported browsers.

honestResidualBoundary: Text to Lattice is a bounded demonstrator, not the full Lattice profile and not a universal conformance oracle.
Source tests and deterministic manifests prove repository behavior and bytes; they do not prove deployed configuration or external service behavior.
Local inference still downloads executable third-party artifacts and reveals ordinary transport metadata to their hosts.
No browser page can guarantee prevention of screenshots, extensions, developer tools, accessibility extraction, cameras, or operating-system capture.
The public endpoint can bound exact downstream work but cannot guarantee a global free-tier Worker-invocation ceiling against distributed hostile traffic.
Accessibility, comprehension, semantic fidelity across uncontrolled prose, and operational reliability require continuing empirical evidence.
